- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.20+), model underreacts; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 1–3% upward adjustment.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show model overestimating, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-term volatility; add 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive or neutral in last 5 days.
